name: Modified Tardieu Scale

instrument.construct: velocity-dependent response to passive stretch with angle and quality-of-reaction recording
instrument.measurement_level: per muscle/joint; mixed ordinal reaction grade plus angular measurements
instrument.version_warning: Published MTS variants differ in QMR category count and wording; the version used must be recorded and not silently converted.

rmd.purpose: assesses muscle response to stretch at given velocities

speed_definitions.V2: speed of limb falling under gravity

angle_structure.R1: angle of muscle reaction/catch during rapid stretch
angle_structure.R2: full passive range measured at very slow speed

rights.basis: RMD reports Cost=Free and describes the measurement procedure. This review did not identify a sufficiently authoritative explicit Public Domain/owner reproduction statement for the complete MTS wording. Rawafid therefore provides an original recording/calculation sheet and paraphrased procedural cues, not a mirrored third-party guide or claimed official form.
rights.excluded_material: Copyrighted third-party application guides, layouts, photographs, training content, and exact proprietary wording are not reproduced.

arabic.rawafid_status: operational Arabic recording and explanatory wording only
arabic.note: No independent validated Arabic MTS translation/form was verified in this review.

evidence.note: Upper-limb adult neurological MTS validity/reliability review; supports cautious interpretation and protocol standardization.
RMD summarizes stroke reliability and measurement error for R1, R2 and R2-R1; population- and muscle-specific values must not be generalized.
Tardieu can help distinguish dynamic neural response from contracture-related passive range when interpreted with R1/R2 and context; it is not a standalone mechanistic diagnosis.

guardrails: Do not create a total MTS score across muscles or joints.
Do not convert a QMR 0-4 version to a 0-5 version or vice versa without a documented mapping from the source protocol.
Do not compute R2-R1 unless R1 and R2 use the same axis, position, side, joint convention and units.
Do not infer walking-phase spasticity or treatment need from MTS alone.
Record speed, position, assessor, assistance, pain and protocol version at each visit.
